title: This Bird Copies Camera Shutters and Car Alarms Perfectly
subject: superb lyrebird

scenes.text: This bird can sing a car alarm, and nobody taught it.
It is a male lyrebird, and it can copy a camera shutter, a motor drive, even power tools.
In the wild it also copies up to twenty other bird species, and it matches their local accents.
The secret is its voice box. It has the most complexly muscled syrinx of any songbird.
Females never mimic. One study suggests they prefer males who copy more species, more accurately.
So that camera click is a love song. A bird is trying to impress you.

description:
A male lyrebird can copy camera shutters, car alarms and other birds.
The secret is the most complexly muscled voice box of any songbird.
Which sound would you teach it?
first_comment: Which sound should a lyrebird learn next? Your ringtone, a doorbell, or a dial-up modem?
